findings.reason: a later reader cannot open the §6 gate log once §3 lands, so the declared log location must move to a durable path, which changes what the section instructs its node to do.
findings.text: §6 places every log "under the run directory", but §3 in the same plan removes a run directory once nothing can still need it (a day of grace by default, plan.html:82-86) and names as durable only the run's ledger row, committed run record and evidence fragment — the gate logs §6 writes are none of those, so the node's own gate evidence is deleted about a day after it lands

findings.reason: the archive is the section's stated justification for deleting a store other readers may still want, so §4's done-when should carry an assertion that the dated archive exists and is non-empty.
findings.text: §4's mechanism is that the files "are compressed into one dated archive under the crew home and removed" (plan.html:102-103), but its done-when checks only the dry-run listing, that the real run removes exactly that list, and that the copy's `crew/watch/` holds under 1 MB — nothing asserts the archive exists or holds the removed bytes, so a sweep that deletes without archiving satisfies every clause

findings.reason: a node dispatched to §4 must invent both the sweep's home and its integration point, and the plan's own third reasoning check requires the production caller be named.
findings.text: §4 names no implementation site for its sweep: §3 extends "the retention pass in `reckon/crew/gc.py`" (plan.html:87), §6 names `_supervisor_exit_record` in `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py` (plan.html:130), and §7 names an hourly user timer over the §3 pass (plan.html:146), while §4 names no module, command or caller

findings.reason: the path is named in §1's own 200-directory sample, my scan is a different and partial instrument; flagged so the author confirms the removed-path list, not because I have falsified it.
findings.text: §6's removed-path set includes a per-run `cache/` tree "a worker's tools fill (matplotlib, xdg, numba)" (plan.html:127-128); I could not reproduce it: of the 400 most recently modified run directories under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/`, none held a top-level `cache/` or `.cache`, and the only top-level `cache/` I opened from the wider population (`r-20261014T013636329481-carrier-agreement`) held a worker's own zarr lock files, not matplotlib, xdg or numba caches
